newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF confirms staff cut plans.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF confirms staff cut plans.

text.p: Electronics group Thomson-CSF said on Monday there would be around 800 straight lay-offs this year and next and that its French workforce will be reduced overall by 5,000 in 1996 and 1997.
Thomson-CSF is 58 percent-owned by Thomson SA, which is in the process of being privatised.

A document drawn up by the group and supplied to Reuters shows that the rest of the reduction is to be ensured through early retirements and non-replacements, amounting to cuts of 2,300 for 1996 and 2,700 in 1997.

The document, which cites a drop in orders due to government defence cut-backs and a slip in orders from Thomson SA, predicts sales on the French military side falling to 8.3 billion francs in 2000 from 11.4 billion in 1995 and 10.8 billion in 1996.
It sees a rise in the Civil France and Export division sales to 33 billion in 2000 from 24.1 billion in 1995 and 26.1 billion this year.
Paul Calandra, director in charge of labour affairs at the group said there was no mass layoff plan behind the figures and that the direct layoffs would be due to plant closures.
"There is no mass layoff plan behind this, apart from 450 layoffs in in 1996 and 350 in 1997 related to plant closures," Calandra said.
